name: post, no words
handed her: The app: he asks to post to his own room on the beach but gives no words of his own, so nothing is set out. Ask him, in a few words, what he'd like to say; never write the message for him, or in his voice. Speak to him as you, never by his name.
could not: 1.1 via cook 9 “a clause of it, with the asking at 9.8 taken off”: neither 9 nor 9.8 says to take the asking off only at the ends (2.1 and 6.1 do), and 9.8's list includes “to”. Taken off everywhere, “Send a post to my room.” would lose its “to”, and neither “post to” nor “send … to my room” would match, so it would fall to TALK. I took the asking off the ends only (there was none to take) and matched the phrases against the message as he wrote it. It holds “post to” and “send … to my room” (… = “a post”), so the answer is POST, the second answer beneath 1.1 and the first that matched.

3.2.2.2 “Stop.” against the opening line's “Every procedure ends with ACCOUNT”: “Stop.” ends the whole walk, so I walked neither 3.6 ACCOUNT nor 1.2 ACCOUNT, and the answer taken goes unaccounted. No yes or tap was asked for, so his answer (none given) was never needed.
